question: When a free AI model has hidden licence rules, how do we know if we are allowed to use it?
reflection: Open sharing of powerful tools can spread opportunity widely, as long as the terms are clear enough for everyone to use them fairly.

sources.subject: SSI secures $5B NVIDIA deal, Kimi K3 ships 2.8T params, OptMem

one_line: Computing power is the race: Nvidia backs a secretive safety-focused lab, while a huge open model arrives with licence strings attached.

top_stories.title: Nvidia invests in Safe Superintelligence
top_stories.what: Nvidia is investing several billion dollars in Ilya Sutskever's Safe Superintelligence, giving it access to Nvidia's next chips and about ten times more computing power within a year.
top_stories.why: Big bets on long-term safety research show where top talent and money are moving.

top_stories.title: Kimi K3 weights released, with conditions
top_stories.what: Moonshot AI released its 2.8 trillion parameter Kimi K3, but the licence requires a commercial deal for companies with revenue above $20 million a year.
top_stories.why: Open weights do not always mean free for business use, so licences must be read before any client project.

top_stories.title: Simple long-term memory for agents
top_stories.what: A developer released OptMem, which keeps every agent memory in a log and builds a short, compressed summary that the agent reads at the start of each session.
top_stories.why: Simple, readable memory files make it easier to check what an agent remembers about a project.

top_stories.title: Small models get better at agent tasks
top_stories.what: A new 3B model reportedly beats much larger open models on agent tasks, and a coding tool server claims large cuts in token use.
top_stories.why: Smaller, cheaper models make AI tools more affordable for small teams.

saudi_lens.text: Large Saudi entities using open models should check revenue-based licence clauses, as some open models now treat big organisations differently.

idea.title: Open model licence checklist
idea.pitch: Create a one-page checklist that reviews any open model's licence for revenue limits, branding rules and data terms before use.
idea.first_step: Compare the licences of three open models used this year and note every condition.

idea_kids.title: Share with rules
idea_kids.pitch: A classroom game where children share toys under different written rules and talk about which rules feel fair and clear.
idea_kids.first_step: Write four sharing rule cards, from very simple to confusing.
